verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same inequality after three routine rewritings, all of which I checked term by term. (1) Factor 2: the paper's left-hand side carries E²/(2X) and the Lean's pressureDebt integrates squareChange/X, so the Lean quantity is twice the paper's; the bound is stated with an unspecified constant C_m on both sides, so the factor is absorbed. (2) Lower limit: the paper integrates over (0,∞) and the Lean over Ioi K, which agree because HeatTailEdit.switch K X vanishes for X below the switch radius, so squareChange vanishes there. (3) The paper leaves ∫_1^∞ x^{-2A-2} dx unevaluated; it equals 1/(2A+1), and this is exactly the denominator -tailDecay d true - (-1) = 2A + 1 appearing in nuConstant, with numerator tailSize d true = e_K² (= the paper's e_K²) and the K^q = K^{-1} giving the paper's 1/X_K. Derivatives: the paper's ∂_η^m is the Lean's iteratedDerivWithin n … (Icc (-1) 1) eta, taken in the same variable η on the same parameter interval, so no chain-rule reconciliation is needed at this level; the passage from ν-jets to η-jets happens inside etaDebt_jet_bound (line 692). Constants: the paper's C_m depends on m only, and etaConstant d true (-1) n depends on n and on the fixed TailData d, likewise not on K or η.
